sessions.lever: STRUCTURAL: separate the loop sentinel from the red channel and write the loop as `while ((sent = tbl[0]) >= 0)`
sessions.note: THE WIN. Reading target around the inner_check label showed two things the m2c-shaped body got wrong: (a) target keeps the RED CHANNEL and the LOOP SENTINEL in DIFFERENT registers - the body's colour args come from $s7/$s6/$s3 while the sentinel lives in $v0; (b) at the label target reads tbl[0] TWICE, `lh $v0,0($s0)` for the test and `lhu $v1,0($s0)` for the next rect[0]. Our body conflated both into one `r`, which put the label in the wrong place - exactly what the two asmfix rules were compensating for. Giving the sentinel its own variable and writing `while ((sent = tbl[0]) >= 0)` puts the read at the label as target does, supplies the missing THIRD phantom slot, and holds the instruction count at 135: score 41 (HEAD) / 40 (previous candidate) -> 29, with frame 88 / vars 24 / regs 10 / args 24 and 135 insns all exactly target. This is also a SEMANTIC CORRECTION - the old body passed `r` to func_80048A7C, so from the second iteration onward it passed the previous tbl[0] instead of the red channel; target always passes $s7. EXPECTED SIDE EFFECT: the two asmfix rules for this function should become unnecessary; verify at the completion gate. Round 8 then tested the call-arg LUID lever (hoist-call-arg-local-flips-jal-delay) on the remaining scheduling cluster where target computes gpu_LoadImage's args early: naming both args first in the loop block, only the source address, or only the rect pointer are ALL INERT at 29; moving the rect stores after the arg locals regresses to 52 (loses the frame). Also measured: for(;;) forms with an explicit break give 131 insns / 69 - the while-with-assignment form is the one that matches; `sid` combined with the corrected loop overshoots to four slots (vars 32). src/text1a.c reverted; candidate.c updated.

sessions.note: NO MOVEMENT; banked at 29. STEP-0 RESULT (the valuable part): the rotating values are pseudo 76 = r -> $s7 (matches target), 77 = g -> $s6 (matches), 78 = b -> $s2 (target wants $s3), 82 = yoff -> $s3 (wants $s4), 79 = outer -> $s4 (wants $s2). Pseudos 75-84 MUTUALLY CONFLICT - a single clique - so each takes the first free register in allocno-priority order. Ours allocates b, yoff, outer; target's order must be outer, b, yoff. The entire residual is therefore ONE PERMUTATION OF THREE ALLOCNO PRIORITIES, and any lever has to raise `outer` above `b` and push `yoff` last. LEVERS A-C, 10 forms, none flips it: colour birth order b,r,g (32) / g,b,r (39) / r,b,g (29); outer if/else arm swap (31); yoff assigned before xoff in both arms (31); `outer = outer + 1` long form (29 inert); an extra `outer` reference in each arm (29 inert, and contrived - not a form to keep); s16 outer (34, +4 insns); s16 yoff (29 inert). Frame and instruction count stay exact (vars 24 / 135 insns) throughout, so none of these regress the structure - they just do not move the priority order. NOT YET RUN: the ALLOCDBG numbers from the instrumented cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1) which would give the three actual priorities; the sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms ref-lift on `outer` sized against those numbers; and a permuter campaign (clean single-function target, directed PERM_*). src/text1a.c reverted.

sessions.lever: ALLOCDBG allocno-sort numbers from the instrumented cc1, then 6 sized loop respellings
sessions.note: THE GAP IS NOW EXACTLY QUANTIFIED. Instrumented cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, env BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1; driver tmp/allocdbg.sh, extractor tmp/allocpick.py) with the candidate applied gives: b = pseudo 78, $s2, nrefs 7, livelen 60, pri 2333; yoff = pseudo 82, $s3, nrefs 5, livelen 43, pri 2325; outer = pseudo 79, $s4, nrefs 5, livelen 50, pri 2000. pri = floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs/livelen*10000 verified against all three. b > yoff ALREADY HOLDS, so the ONLY requirement is outer > 2333: at livelen 50 that needs floor_log2(n)*n > 11.67, i.e. nrefs 6 -> 2*6/50*10000 = 2400 (one extra reference is exactly enough), or livelen <= 42 at nrefs 5 -> 2380. A ~17% lift. SIX loop respellings measured, none delivers it: for-loop and while-loop forms (34, and the pseudo numbering shifts); do/while form (34 - it DOES move the priorities to outer 5192 / b 3870 / yoff 5853 but into the WRONG permutation yoff > outer > b); `outer = outer + 1` long form, `switch (outer)` arm selection, and `if (outer != 2)` loop-back all leave the three priorities byte-identical at 2000 / 2333 / 2325. WHY THE SANCTIONED REF-LIFT CANNOT REACH IT: duplicated-statement-into-arms needs a real statement mentioning `outer` duplicated into both arms, but the arms are guarded by `outer == 0` so GCC folds `outer` to a constant in the then-arm and the reference never reaches reg_n_refs - which is exactly why round 9's `yoff = 0xF0 + outer` / `0 * outer` probe was inert. No byte-neutral construct in this body adds an unfoldable sixth reference. NEXT RUNG is the directed permuter; NOT started because a detached campaign must be waited on and harvested in-session (grinder-permuter-orphan-stop-gate) and there was not enough session left to supervise ~20-30k iters. src/text1a.c reverted.
